findings_qualitative.value: First CO detection around a G-type star; HD 121191 CO lies inside the planetesimal belt, possibly due to shielding and viscous spreading

evidence.quote: we detect CO for the first time around the young 10-16 Myr old G1V star HD 129590

claims.hypothesis: Gas can be detected around Sun-like stars
claims.experiment: Band 6 CO 2-1 survey of 10 debris discs
claims.result: CO flux 0.056±0.014 Jy km/s, S/N~4-9 around HD 129590
claims.finding: First CO around a G-type star, mass 2-10e-5 Mearth

evidence.quote: The gas seems colocated with its planetesimal belt and its total mass is likely between $2-10 \times 10^{-5}$ M$_\oplus$.

claims.hypothesis: CO in HD 121191 is colocated with the planetesimals
claims.result: gas at ~22 au vs dust at ~52 au
claims.finding: CO closer in, consistent with shielding and spreading

evidence.quote: find that the CO lies much closer-in than the planetesimals in the system

claims.hypothesis: Exocomets resemble Solar System comets in CO content
claims.experiment: Upper limits on CO mass converted to ice fractions
claims.finding: some systems below Solar System comet range

evidence.quote: the CO content in HD 114082 ($<$1.6%) and HR 4796A ($<$1.9%) is already below the range

why_this_data.value: Targets chosen as bright discs with late spectral types and highest predicted CO detectability

evidence.quote: we prioritised systems with late spectral types (which have less detections so far) and bright debris discs

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: CO near HD 114082 attributed to a line-of-sight cloud rather than circumstellar gas

evidence.quote: might be due to a cloud on the line of sight

limitations_admitted.value: Dust masses have large systematic uncertainties from arbitrary composition; HD 129590 gas unconstrained by MCMC

evidence.quote: it should be understood that it has large systematic uncertainties
